products.name: EasyPair
products.tagline: Nearby sharing with true resume — now with self-updates (Ophelia Update Center)
products.description: Offline file sharing with zero limits — Wi-Fi Direct, hotspot, same Wi-Fi, USB cable or Bluetooth, no router and no data needed. Photos, videos, audio, files, folders, installed apps (APK) and clipboard text. v1.6.1 fixes the resume identity check (fragmented first reads hashed the wrong bytes, so interrupted big transfers restarted from zero), guards truncated small-file saves, and cleans up the group-owner send path. v1.6.0's resume engine, v1.5.0's encrypted TLS receiver and full LocalSend v2 interop are all intact.

notes: Every accepted socket now actually closes (fd leak per transfer fixed), including the RFCOMM server + owner-poll loop.
Dead links can no longer park the receiver forever — read timeouts at every stage.
DoS hardening: frame cap 64MB to 4MB, header/line read caps, Content-Length reads capped.
Device map / history stores are now thread-safe (no more ConcurrentModificationException).
History screens no longer do file IO during composition.
Ophelia Update Center in Settings → About: silent update check on open plus manual 'Check' — downloads are sha-256 verified in-app (same signing key: installs over 1.6.1)
v1 + v2 signature schemes on the APK — install issues fixed on some devices
Transfers keep priority: an incoming-transfer prompt always wins over the update dialog

RESUME actually resumes: the partial-file head hash was computed with the wrong buffer offsets, so it never matched the sender's proof on fragmented (Bluetooth / slow Wi-Fi) reads — resume silently fell back to restart-from-zero. The hash math is fixed and unit-tested
A dropped small file is now reported as failed (connection dropped at X of Y) instead of being saved as a truncated 'success'
Wi-Fi Direct group-owner sends no longer push 0-byte extras; the About card shows the real version
NEW: PARTIAL-FILE RESUME — interrupted transfers continue from the exact byte, never from zero
Big files (8 MB+) are received into a private .part buffer; a drop at 80% of a video keeps those bytes safe
RESUME TRANSFER card on Home + Queue after a failed batch — one tap and only the missing tail travels
Same-file proof: first-4KB SHA-256 must match, so a different file with the same name can never corrupt a partial; stale partials (14 days) self-clean
NEW: ENCRYPTED RECEIVER — flip 'Encrypted receiver (HTTPS)' in Settings and EasyPair itself serves LocalSend behind TLS
Certificate is generated in the Android Keystore (hardware-backed where available); the private key never leaves your phone
Our announcement now carries the certificate's real SHA-256 — LocalSend and EasyPair senders PIN us, nothing travels in the clear
Default OFF (LocalSend's own default): plain-HTTP interop keeps working exactly as before until you opt in
NEW: ENCRYPTED LOCALSEND — LocalSend receivers that enable HTTPS mode are now supported
REAL certificate pinning: the announced SHA-256 fingerprint must match the presented certificate or the handshake is refused — never trust-all
Encrypted peers show a lock + 'encrypted' badge in the nearby device list
8 new tests including a real self-signed HTTPS server round-trip (pinned pass / wrong-pin reject / unpinned reject)
NEW: LocalSend interop — receive from the LocalSend app on Windows/macOS/Linux/iOS/Android (multicast discovery 224.0.0.167, HTTP REST v2.2 on port 53317)
NEW: send TO any LocalSend receiver over HTTP REST (prepare-upload + upload, both wire generations supported)
NEW: incoming LocalSend files verified with SHA-256 when the sender provides a hash, saved to Downloads/LocalSend and listed in Received Files
27 new JVM protocol tests; gesture/UI untouched — same look, same flow
